a04c5ebf319caf6f280410eb26a0eb48310aa9d5: Alpe Cermis is a modest, low-key resort with 24 km of runs, offering an intimate skiing experience far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Alpe Cermis's family-friendly reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Alpe Cermis's altitude (860 m at the bottom, 2250 m at the top) helps it keep a decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Alpe Cermis is clearly on the expensive side: 71€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short, Alpe Cermis doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

a0c6dcb49720d000681a469851bc4fc102bed5ab: Arvieux-en-Queyras is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 12 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Arvieux-en-Queyras has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Arvieux-en-Queyras's altitude (1150 m at the base, 2100 m at the top) helps it keep decent snow through midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. With a day lift pass at just 20€, Arvieux-en-Queyras is one of the most affordable destinations in France. For families on a tight budget, or skiers who want to fit in lots of days without breaking the bank, it's a sincere and often overlooked choice. In short: Arvieux-en-Queyras doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
